tests.mutation: In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; CoverRules.Degree read the Three-Quarters row as needing 80 per cent (`covered >= 80`), so an object covering three-quarters gave Half Cover; this test went red, and so did attack-modifiers' test of the step's answer.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; CoverRules.Degree gave Half Cover to an object covering anything at all (`covered >= 0` for `covered >= CoveringObstacle.Half`); this test went red and no other did.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; CoverRules.Degree read a creature by the object rows (`if (false && obstacle.Kind == Obstacle.Creature)`), so a creature covering 80 per cent gave Three-Quarters Cover and one covering 30 per cent gave none; this test went red, and so did the creature-below-half decline and attack-modifiers' decline.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; CoverRules.Degree dropped the entry's question from the decline (the "Another creature" limb out of Attempted); this test went red and no other did. It went red too under the creature-read-as-an-object mutation above, which answered where the corpus does not choose.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; CoverRules.Degree answered from the first of several stated sources of cover (`obstacles.Count > 99` for `obstacles.Count > 1`); this test went red and no other did.
In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; the CoverDegree handler defaulted missing Obstacles to `[]`; this test went red and no other did.
